office_does: One of nine statewide-elected justices on Washington's court of last resort, deciding appeals, state constitutional questions, and the rules that govern every court in the state.
race_blurb: Chief Justice Debra Stephens, on the court since 2008, led the August primary with 54.5% against Tacoma tax attorney and Navy veteran Todd Bloom (27.2%), who has never held judicial office and criticizes the court's McCleary, Quinn and natural-gas initiative rulings.

candidates.summary: Chief Justice and a justice since 2008, formerly a Court of Appeals judge and Gonzaga appellate lawyer and professor. She describes a text-and-structure method applied to a constitution written as a broad framework, and wrote McCleary.
highlights: On the court since 2008, Chief Justice since January 2025 [S1][S7]
Wrote McCleary (2012), recognizing a positive constitutional right to amply funded K-12 education [S2][S6]
Wrote the 6-3 majority striking Initiative 2066 on single-subject grounds [S4][S10]
Describes "respect for text and structure" and admires Justice Brennan's view that "rights without remedies are hollow" [S9]
Endorsed by all other sitting justices and 150+ judges; first in the primary with 54.50% [S3][S7]

judicial.basis: Constitution as a broad framework applied with fidelity to purposes, broader state protections, Brennan's 'rights without remedies are hollow', and authorship of McCleary; her stated respect for text and structure keeps it at +1. Unchanged from the primary.

experience.basis: Eighteen years on the court, current Chief Justice, prior Court of Appeals service and the whole court's endorsement; unchanged from the primary.

candidates.summary: Tacoma tax and business attorney, CPA and Navy veteran who serves on the WSBA Board of Governors and has never held judicial office. He runs on judicial restraint and criticizes several of the court's major rulings.
highlights: Says judges should "faithfully apply the law as written" and exercise "judicial restraint" [S3][S10]
Says Quinn was "wrongly decided" and the McCleary contempt sanctions overstepped the separation of powers [S4][S7]
Also says judges must consider how rulings are received and give more weight to voter-approved measures [S7]
No judicial service; FINRA arbitrator 1999-2020 and active-duty Navy officer 2002-2013 [S1]
Recommended by the state Republican Party; second in the primary with 27.20% [S5][S8]

judicial.basis: Repeated restraint and as-written statements and criticism of McCleary and Quinn; medium, not high, because he also says judges must weigh how rulings will be received. Unchanged from the primary.

experience.basis: No judicial service and frames the race as a choice to 'give someone new your vote'; unchanged from the primary.
